The single-pair theorem is general and non-vacuous; the triangle theorem is a fixed three-Bool instance; the many-conflict statement (conflict graph, proper colouring, a 3-clique needs three colours) exists only as prose in paper.md section 9. This node proves the colouring characterisation, the odd-closed-walk obstruction and the fibre bit count in Lean for arbitrary relations/finite types, and tabulates all labelled graphs on up to 5 vertices natively. The sha256 of the three bound source files matches their operad pins (Paper.lean b0f6365d, Paper001.lean b9034069, DerivationDagQMClosure.lean c9ad9c23); the DerivationDagQMClosure theorem pg_to_sn_and_wdp_route_chain_composition is a conjunction of fixed arithmetic facts and does not mention refinement, so it supplies nothing here.
independent_predicates: Union-find components and breadth-first two-colouring replace the producer's depth-first components and exhaustive tag enumeration; proper one-bit tags counted as 2^components when bipartite.
Chromatic number by dynamic programming over vertex subsets (cover by independent sets), minimal bits as bit_length(chi-1); the producer uses backtracking colourings with 2^b colours.
Odd girth as the least odd k with nonzero trace of A^k; the producer uses breadth-first levels.
Enumeration identity: sum over bipartite G of 2^c(G) equals sum_k C(n,k) 2^(k(n-k)); labelled bipartite count equals graphs with at most one bit.

Injective tag counts as falling factorials (2^b)_m; refinement records recomputed by evaluating the refinement on every (q, t, a, b) in the checker and compared with the closed forms n(n-1) o^(n-1) t^(n-1) (t-1) and n(n-1) o^(n-1) (o-1) t^n; exact Python/Rust wire equality and literal Lean axiom reports.

claim_boundary.supports: Kernel-checked and general over all types A, O, T: the refined report (q, t) keeps q as its first projection; a differing tag separates a pair (the source theorem refine_separates is this forward direction only); on a pair the old report collapses, the tag decides separation exactly (refine_separates_iff, new); refinement never merges what q separated. For a conflict relation C contained in the collapse of q: a GIVEN tag resolves every conflict iff it is proper for C (resolves_iff_proper); SOME b-bit tag (Fin b -> Bool) resolves every conflict iff C has a proper 2^b-colouring (refine_separates_many, an existence statement over tags). A Bool tag proper for C forbids any odd closed walk in C (so no triangle, no 5-cycle); this is the forward direction only, the converse (no odd closed walk implies a one-bit tag, Konig) is not in the kernel and is used natively (bipartite iff odd girth 0; one-bit tags 2^components when bipartite). For a finite type A in which every pair of distinct elements conflicts (a collapsed fibre taken as its own type, or q constant) a b-bit tag separating all pairs exists iff |A| <= 2^b (fibre_bits_iff; one bit iff |A| <= 2, fibre_one_bit_iff); for the fibre {a // q a = x} of an arbitrary report q some b-bit tag on the whole type resolves all conflicts between distinct fibre elements iff the fibre has at most 2^b elements (fibre_report_bits_iff). Native columns are counts over all (q, t) and ordered pairs (a, b), a = b allowed: quadruples = o^n t^n n^2; separated_by_tag = pairs with q a = q b and t a != t b; refined_equal = pairs with equal refined reports; old_separation_kept = pairs with q a != q b (all stay separated); iff_failures = pairs where equality of refined reports differs from equality of both components (0; the checker evaluates the refinement itself). Exact native tables: 14 named conflict graphs (components, proper one-bit tag counts 2^c or 0, chromatic number, minimal bits, odd girth), all labelled graphs on 1..5 vertices (labelled bipartite counts 1,2,7,41,376; minimal-bit distributions), fibre tag counts for m=1..5 and bits for m=6,8,9,17, and refinement counts for five small (n,o,t).
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Any algorithm, complexity or guarantee for FINDING a tag (the tables and the iff are existence statements, not search procedures); which tag a host should supply; the converse of the odd-closed-walk theorem in the kernel (Konig; native only); conflict graphs on more than 5 vertices beyond the 14 named ones; infinite carriers; any measurement, physical or interpretive reading of tags.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: For a report q and a conflict relation C inside its collapse, SOME b-bit tag resolves all conflicts iff C has a proper 2^b-colouring (refine_separates_many); a GIVEN tag resolves C iff it is proper (resolves_iff_proper). The source refine_separates is the forward direction for one pair; refine_separates_iff is the one-pair equivalence on collapsed pairs.
claim_boundary.next_test: First prove in Lean the converse of no_one_bit_of_odd_cycle (a finite symmetric conflict relation with no odd closed walk has a proper Bool tag), then that breadth-first 2-colouring is sound and complete for deciding it, as the first algorithmic statement about finding a tag; the present node proves existence criteria only.

colour_meanings.Report: Function q from the carrier to observations
colour_meanings.Tag: Supplied function t from the carrier to tag values (Bool, Fin b -> Bool, Fin k)
colour_meanings.RefinedReport: Pair report a |-> (q a, t a)
colour_meanings.ConflictRelation: Relation C on the carrier whose pairs must be separated
colour_meanings.Verdict: Boolean: tag is proper for C
colour_meanings.BitCount: Least number of tag bits resolving C

relation_evidence.many_conflicts_iff_proper_colouring: Kernel theorem for arbitrary relations; native bipartite counts 1,2,7,41,376 agree with the colouring-pair identity.
relation_evidence.odd_closed_walk_refuses_one_bit: Kernel theorem; every native graph with positive odd girth has zero one-bit tags.

review.reviewed_target_qualification: The DAG phrase "satisfying many conflicts at once ... unaddressed" is narrowed: existence of a satisfying b-bit tag for conflicts inside a collapse is exactly proper 2^b-colourability (kernel-checked); finding such a tag remains unaddressed.
